csi_deployment.publisher_service:
[Unit]
Description=Agent Computer trusted Candidate CSI publisher
After=ac-k3s.service
Requires=ac-k3s.service
Wants=agent-computer-csi-registrar.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
Group=root
# Set NODE_NAME to the exact Kubernetes node name in this operator-owned file.
EnvironmentFile=/etc/agent-computer/csi.env
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/install -d -m 0700 /var/lib/agent-computer-csi
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/install -d -m 0755 /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi.agent-computer.io /var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/agent-computer-csi ${NODE_NAME}
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2
UMask=0077
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateMounts=no
# Do not add filesystem sandbox directives creating a separate mount namespace:
# publication must be visible to Kubelet and the local execution controller.
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX
LimitNOFILE=8192

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
csi_deployment.registrar_service:
[Unit]
Description=Agent Computer CSI registration using upstream node-driver-registrar
After=agent-computer-csi.service
Requires=agent-computer-csi.service
PartOf=agent-computer-csi.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
Group=root
# Install an operator-verified upstream registrar; the component evidence pins
# the tested image digest and extracted executable checksum.
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/csi-node-driver-registrar --csi-address=/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi.agent-computer.io/csi.sock --kubelet-registration-path=/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi.agent-computer.io/csi.sock --plugin-registration-path=/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2
UMask=0077
NoNewPrivileges=true
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

verified_behaviors: Actual restricted gVisor Pods use inline CSI, with no hostPath or direct backing subPath. Live node guards and database startup admission match the complete front-mount reference and prepared Candidate.

Same UID/volume/target retry leaves the mount unchanged. A fully consistent replacement UID/target request is rejected by the original durable claim. Publisher restart preserves the same active mount.
Nine actual CSI registrations match final-run Pod UIDs and are durably revoked. Recovery provides no IO seal and does not recreate any mount or grant.

Controller SIGKILL disconnects FUSE. An already-open descriptor rejects a new write with EIO/ENOTCONN while stopped PID 1 remains for the original independent cgroup deadline. This observation is not a drain receipt.

Kubelet unpublish and explicit duplicate cleanup work with dead source mounts. A foreign replacement bind is retained and rejected; revoked/foreign/replacement requests fail. UID/GID 1000 with no supplementary groups cannot connect to the CSI endpoint.
A separate read-only JuiceFS process with zero data cache reads five expected Candidate files. Independent Python signed S3 GETs revalidate twenty references from five output manifests.
All eleven executions remain Unknown with Draining leases; no candidate writer drain or completion rows are produced.
experiment_notes: No registered repo-sandbox targets were available; the verified test environment was a task-owned QEMU VM (4 vCPU, 6 GiB RAM, 24 GiB sparse overlay).
Public crates.io TLS downloads failed. Cargo/Bazel used public mirror archives verified against official locked SHA-256 values through task-local distdirs; TLS and dependency checks were retained.

An initial direct Rust plugin-registration service received Kubelet PROTOCOL_ERROR. It was replaced by the upstream node-driver-registrar; the final qualified flow uses the standard separate registration and CSI sockets.

Actual fuser direct root mounts report type fuse. Publication checks use that observed type together with device/root/source identity. Both before and after attachment the clone is made private, since a shared host parent otherwise introduces a new peer group.

The previous PID-1-stop fixture required writes after controller death. It now first proves the stopped-init writer is active, then verifies old-FD write rejection after controller death while retaining the original cgroup deadline assertion.

Earlier failing development cases were left conservative. The final run uses a new organization and exact execution/instance test selectors; one earlier Error Pod was still present before the disposable VM was reclaimed.
VM collection independently checked final executable hashes, records, raw storage reads and absence of final-run Pods. Private overlay, SSH keys and VM cloud-init files were removed after collection.

limits: Computer ready remains false; T01-T43 remain not_run. Public execution capability and accepted completion remain pending.
The mount-local barrier does not revoke trusted direct backing writers, legacy direct mounts or process/network effects. It is not a multi-node or power-loss fence.
Serialized references, output reports and observed empty cgroups cannot recreate live seal authority or release a lease. Controller loss may leave in-flight backing IO unresolved.

Only the qualified Linux host mount namespace, K3s/containerd/runsc stack, fixed Kubelet path and documented basic filesystem operations are covered. No general App checkpoint, HA or broad application filesystem compatibility is claimed.
Durable registry tombstones and private state are retained without automatic reclamation. Production installation and backing store qualification remain operator responsibilities.
The live fixture uses isolated-VM HTTP for its S3 endpoint, not a production TLS qualification.
